thread:
support-lee: Customer reported sporadic 400s ("dimension mismatch") on /v1/embeddings and tail latencies hitting 3-4s. Happens during client spikes; they also saw 401s during token rotation earlier. Full details below.

maria: Can you paste a minimal request and the error body? my hunch is mixed-dim vectors in a single batched payload.

kevin: Runtime note: our coalescer merges small requests up to the dynamic window (20ms by default). If a client sends a batched array with one malformed vector, we currently forward the whole batch — backend rejects and we surface a 400. That can also amplify tail latency when retries pile up.

aj: Customer sample (redacted) — they send an array of vectors of different lengths. Example: 
```
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"r-instruct-embed-1536","input":[[0.1,...1536 values...],[0.2,...768 values...]]}'
```
Response: `HTTP/1.1 400`
```
{"error":"dimension mismatch: expected 1536, got 768 at index 1"}
```

sre-bot: Incident #3421 created: spike at 2026-02-15T14:32Z. Related: token-rotation 401s were reported for ~30s and caused a brief retry storm which increased coalescing.

maria: Repro steps I used locally: spin up 50 concurrent clients, each sending 10 tiny requests rapidly and occasionally bundling one malformed vector into the batch. Use dyn_window=25ms and max_batch_size=64 to trigger coalescing. Observed: single malformed item causes whole batch rejection and tail latency spikes as clients retry.

kevin: Short-term mitigations:
- front-proxy should validate per-item shapes and return 400 per-request before batching (fast fail)
- reduce tenant max_batch_size to limit blast radius (eg set to 8)
- make retries exponential with jitter client-side to avoid synchronized backoff

aj: Billing note: customer reported double-charging for retries (original request + retry). support-lee: please confirm which retries result in billable tokens.

support-lee: Confirmed: retries that successfully complete are billable; failed 400s are not billed but some client libraries re-send and get billed. Recommended: refund obvious duplicate charges and advise client to implement idempotency keys.

jess: Quick repro script (python) to share with SRE/QA: 
```python
import requests, json, threading

URL = 'https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings'
HEADERS = {'Authorization': 'Bearer ' + 'REDACTED', 'Content-Type':'application/json'}

def send_batch(bad=False):
    normal = [ [0.0]*1536 for _ in range(3) ]
    if bad:
        # inject a different-dim vector among correct ones
        normal[1] = [0.0]*768
    payload = {'model':'r-instruct-embed-1536', 'input': normal}
    r = requests.post(URL, headers=HEADERS, data=json.dumps(payload))
    print(r.status_code, r.text[:200])

threads = []
for i in range(50):
    t = threading.Thread(target=send_batch, args=(i%10==0,))
    t.start(); threads.append(t)
for t in threads: t.join()
```

kevin: I've pushed a canary that performs per-item shape validation and returns 400 at the proxy layer (staging). Rolling to prod after smoke tests. Also PR open to make coalescer split around bad items instead of forwarding whole batch.

support-lee: Action items:
- eng-runtime (kevin) to roll the fast-fail proxy canary to prod and PR for splitting batches.
- support (aj, lee) to offer refund for duplicate charges and share the repro script with the customer.
- devex (maria) to update docs: recommend per-request validation and how to set tenant max_batch_size / dyn window.

jess: +1. Also suggest enabling tenant-level `priority_tags` so customer small requests avoid being coalesced with larger bulk jobs.

maria: Follow-up note: this is an edge-case but high-severity for some customers. Recommend a short kb article and a small CLI check tool to validate vector shapes before sending.

support-lee: Thanks team — will update the customer with mitigations (lower max_batch_size, try idempotency keys, apply refund). :thumbsup:
